items.quote: seconds = seconds + math.max(0, objective.need - (objective.have or 0)) * 4
items.what: The work estimate (4 seconds per objective count, 10 seconds per giver talk) exists twice: named in Planning/Laps.lua:58-61 (RUN, WORK_YARDS = 4 * RUN, TALK_YARDS = 10 * RUN, canonical) and as bare 4 and 10 in Session.Work (Core/Session.lua:45-60).
items.why: Both size the same thing, how long a step's work takes, one for lap worth and one for the session budget. Differences: Laps scales by WorkFactor for above-level quests and counts max(1, need); Session counts need minus have and returns nil for explore or unknown counts. Those look intentional (different questions), but the per-count and per-talk seconds are the same tuning values and Session's are unnamed, so retuning Laps leaves the session estimate behind.
items.reason: The two estimates serve different contracts and share only two literals: Planning/Laps.lua:164-180 weighs a new quest's XP per yard (total need, WorkFactor, one TALK_YARDS of 10 s for a quest's pickup and hand-in together), while Session.Work budgets remaining counts in seconds at 10 s per checklist row (tests/session_spec.lua:48 'ten seconds per interaction'), so the 10 is not the same quantity and retuning the lap weight does not make the session estimate wrong. What remains is one bare `* 4`, the Settled 'One-line idioms' shape and the lens's small-idiom exclusion; an unnamed number is not a second implementation.
